  <description>Cerri is an elf who goes against everything elves are known for. She isn't drop dead gorgeous, she doesn't exude an air of confidence, she doesn't hold her head high and sway her hips as she walks. Rather, she is covered in marks and bruises, more often than not mud and dirt cover her face and cake in her hair, and she carries the scent of blood with her. Never without her hand crafted longbow or it's equivalent dagger twin.</description>
  <background>What started as a simple experiment, ended in complete and utter failure. The premise was simple, create someone who would be self sufficient in any situation, capable of surviving in the harshest conditions on their own for extremely long periods of time.

Failure was seemingly decided from the start. A stupid mistake meant that the usual techniques used to maintain a transhumans essence failed catastrophically. These were the early days of transhumans, so Re-Do's weren't exactly on the list. With no other subjects, the decision was made to make do with what they had. Raising the girl inside of simulations that taught her how to hunt and track animals by sound and scent.

One of these didn't work either. Born with working ears, 01's hearing quickly disappeared, by three she was completely deaf and incapable of having it simply restored. Another silly mistake that fried the nerves in her ears. Repair was possible, but long, expensive, and not worth the investment.

The next step in the master plan was to toss the girl into a forest and recover her corpse later, recycling what they could with her body. This was the third mistake.

The girl may not have been able to hear, but she retained all of the information she was taught. She knew how to track by scent, she could differentiate species by their urine, she knew where to strike animals to preserve the pelts, where the best cuts of meat were, and how to use every part of a corpse to it's absolute potential.

In short, this meant she didn't die.

Scouting parties looked for the girl for years. Fifteen years, before they finally found her camp. Embers were still burning in the small concealed fire she kept. The party, a group of four Subject Retrieval Units set out to find 01, she had to be close.

She was, closer than they expected. Four arrows and, what amounted to a sharpened bone to the jugular marked this girl as the Apex Predator. She killed the retrieval units, believing them to be a new type of game to hunt. Not fond of the taste, she decided Humans made for lousy prey. But she set out in search of more to hunt anyway, because they put up a challenge to hunt.

It was somewhere around this time that she established contact with Father Canston. It was an odd meeting, because she had loosed an arrow straight into his heart, but when she moved in to skin the kill, he was still alive. Some part of the girl, deep down inside, switched. What might be described as "Humanity" "Maternal Instincts" or even "God Himself" compelled the girl to nurse Canston back to health. As she did he taught her things. How to speak in his native tongue, how to use her hands to communicate, and how to read the lips of the rest of the world. He taught her about civilisation, and people, and how the world worked.

He told her about shadowrunners as a form of bedtime story, and she hung off every word. "That's what I want to do. I want to kill the gods" she smiled at him. He had explained god, but she had brushed it off as the vague figures she remembered from her earlier years in life. Little more than large white blurs, she hadn't known that they were people. But she knew, somehow. Again, call it instinct, that they were related to the megas.

And she had never tasted God.</background>

      <notes>GREMLINS
BONUS: 4 KARMA
PER LEVEL (MAX 4)
Characters with the Gremlins quality don’t get along with technology. Devices malfunction inexplicably,
software crashes unexpectedly, vehicles refuse to start,
components become unusually fragile at his touch, and wireless links suffer faltering connections and odd interference whenever he’s involved.
For each level (maximum of 4), reduce the number of rolled 1s necessary to get a glitch (p. 45) by 1 whenever the character is attempting to use a moderately sophisticated device. For example, a character with a dice pool of 8 and Gremlins level 2 (8 Karma) would trigger a glitch if two or more 1s result from the test (instead of the normal 4). The gamemaster may also require the character to make a test for operation that would otherwise succeed automatically to see whether or not a glitch occurs.
When describing the effects of a Gremlin-induced glitch, gamemasters should play up the notion of a particularly weird mechanical or electronics malfunction.
Some examples of Gremlin-induced glitches include:
the magazine falling out of a pistol when attempting a critical shot, a keypad inexplicably burning out while entering a code to disarm an alarm system, or the commlink interface converting to Sperethiel mid-sentence when attempting to access a restricted node.
Note that Gremlins is a Negative quality—its effects hinder the character (and probably entertain others). The character cannot use his Gremlins quality to damage an opponent’s high-tech equipment merely by touching it.
Anything the character attempts to sabotage using only Gremlins will function flawlessly. (Obviously, he can try any ordinary means of sabotage, but Gremlins will haunt his efforts.)
The effect only applies to external equipment and does not affect cyberware, bioware, or other implants.
</notes>

Note that Gremlins is a Negative quality—its effects hinder the character (and probably entertain others). The character cannot use his Gremlins quality to damage an opponent’s high-tech equipment merely by touching it.
Anything the character attempts to sabotage using only Gremlins will function flawlessly. (Obviously, he can try any ordinary means of sabotage, but Gremlins will haunt his efforts.)
The effect only applies to external equipment and does not affect cyberware, bioware, or other implants.
</notes>
